name: Meshach
bio: Mishael, renamed Meshach by the Babylonians, was one of Daniel's three companions taken into exile. Like Daniel, he refused to defile himself with the king's food, thriving instead on a diet of vegetables and water (Daniel 1:1-21). When Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and commanded everyone to worship it, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused despite the threat of a fiery furnace, declaring that even if God did not save them, they would not bow to another god. Thrown into the blazing furnace, they emerged completely unharmed, not even smelling of smoke, after a figure "like the Son of God" appeared with them in the flames; Nebuchadnezzar then promoted all three (Daniel 3:1-30). He is a different figure from Mishael son of Uzziel, Aaron's cousin.
